item.description: The number includes 890 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.

item.title: Russia launches rare daytime mass drone attack on Ukraine, around 200 already reportedly shot down
item.description: "I suppose we will see some more missiles today,"‌‌ Defense Ministry advisor Serhii Flash said.

item.title: Ukraine believes Tucker Carlson 'works for Putin' amid growing US scrutiny
item.description: Tucker Carlson, a conservative commentator now under scrutiny in the U.S., has long drawn criticism in Ukraine for amplifying narratives aligned with the Kremlin — a record that is gaining fresh attention as he claims he could face criminal charges at home. item.title: Ukraine 'liquidates' hitman working for Russia's GRU, thwarts plot to assassinate high-profile figures, SBU says
item.description: "Thanks to the SBU. I'm fine. Unlike the hitman. Russia should burn," Serhii Sternenko wrote on Telegram on March 24.

item.title: From Tehran to Kyiv: Ukraine’s Iranian diaspora live through war while watching another
item.description: With air raid sirens and missile strikes part of daily life in Kyiv, many Iranians living in Ukraine found themselves watching another crisis unfold in their homeland — one that feels both distant and painfully familiar. Following the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran and the assassination of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, along with several senior figures of the regime, members of the small Iranian community in Kyiv say they are following events closely, balancing hope for political change with fear

item.title: Ukraine's military destroys Russian Zircon missile launcher in occupied Crimea
item.description: Ukrainian forces destroyed a Zircon hypersonic missile launcher in occupied Crimea during an overnight strike March 24, Ukraine's military intelligence agency said.

item.title: General Staff: Russia has lost 1,280,960 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022
item.description: The number includes 1,220 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.

item.title: Ukraine's air defense downs 97% of Russian kamikaze drones in rare mass daytime strike
item.description: While nighttime mass Russian drone strikes are an almost nightly occurrence, daytime assaults are far less common.

item.title: Russian government ordered Moscow internet blackout, The Bell reports
item.description: According to The Bell's sources, the Scientific and Technical Service Department of the Russian Security Service (FSB) received orders "from above" to shutdown the internet in response to unspecified security threats.

item.title: Russian military icebreaker damaged in unprecedented Baltic Sea drone strike, Ukraine claims
item.description: The ship, identified by the General Staff as patrol icebreaker "Pruga," was docked at a shipyard in Vyborg when it was hit, the General Staff said.

item.title: Latvia, Estonia say drones that strayed into their territory overnight were Ukrainian
item.description: One drone was reported to have landed and exploded in a field in Lativia's Kraslava region, while another struck the chimney of the Auvere power station near the Russian border.

item.title: Loss and loneliness in a contemporary Moldovan classic
item.description: From the early pages of "The Summer My Mother Had Green Eyes," we are swimming in the protagonist Aleksy's grief. The story begins at a point in his late teenage years when he "hated (his mother) more than ever," and could have "killed her with a thought." She is not a source of love and strength in his life — that is, the woman who gave him life — but of utter repulsion and shame. item.title: Ukraine preparing 'key changes' to mobilization, AWOL policy, defense minister says after meeting infantrymen
item.description: The announcement came after Mykhailo Fedorov met with assault soldiers and infantrymen from 13 different units fighting across the front line.

item.title: The success of Ukraine's drone industry, explained
item.description: The Kyiv Independent’s Kollen Post sits down with Oleksandr Yakovenko, founder of TAF Industries, to discuss how his company went from wartime volunteer logistics to becoming one of Ukraine’s largest drone manufacturers.

item.title: Ukraine’s wartime businesses turn to foreign markets
item.description: As war reshapes Ukraine’s economy, small businesses are turning to foreign markets to survive, grow, and build long-term resilience.
